chapter: Young players, Coltrane and the avant-garde
title: Coltrane shows his chord chart at home
summary: Sam and Yusef Lateef visit Coltrane, who explains his chart of chords around each key.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: I think he let that "love supreme" ...go a little too far, you know.

You see, Coltrane knew what he was doing you see, and the guys was playing with him knew what he was doing, because he taught them, you know. So, uh, Yusef and I went up out to Coltrane's house one night and uh, as usual when we got there he was practicing, man, practicing at the piano, he was down in the basement so he came up with his horn and greeted us, you know, sit down, and started talking to them. So the brother was asking him about, you know, some things on the saxophone you know, some things that he didn't quite understand and he wanted to uh, ask him the facts. So uh, as usual Coltrane was his usual good hearted self, man, so he had a chart, you know, a chart. And in this round circle he had rectangles all the way around, you know, all the way around this chart and in this, these little things was, uh, chords and all kinds of, uh, you know, chord signs and every one of them, and the key at the point, at the top up there, that means like, ....... if he's playing in the key of C, OK, you got the key of C something like that. He had all those chord symbols, man, and their key in that one rectangle man. He could play, you know, in that key, low C, right there. That means that when, that's the reason why he had, when he played the C7 chord you heard a whole lot of stuff, right in that one C7 chord, see because it's all uh, relative to that key of C right there, what he had

in there. And he went all around, all through the keys, just like that. So he explained that to a, to us. Out to his house, man. And so that uh, opened my eyes up and found out what he was doing, you know, and really opened the eyes to, to the brother, you know. So, uh, when I saw a lot of guys out there with saxophones going crazy out there, you know, and listening--see, that stuff made me real tired, because see, they didn't know what the hell they was doing up there man. They didn't know what, what was going on, what this man--because he didn't explain it to them, he explained it to to save the people, you know.
